results.title: GBS prognostic factors

results.finding: Patients requiring MV: 60-70% walk independently at 1 year; 15-20% have permanent disability; 5% mortality
results.title: Severe GBS prognosis

output.summary: Published evidence indicates that severe GBS requiring mechanical ventilation is associated with 60–70% probability of independent walking at 1 year; 15–20% of patients sustain permanent disability; reported mortality is approximately 5%. High anti-GM1 titers and CMAP amplitude reduction (secondary axonal injury) are independently associated with slower and incomplete recovery. Extended inpatient and outpatient rehabilitation is typically required.

avoided_actions.rationale: GBS is a peripheral nerve / nerve-root disorder; EEG has no role in diagnosis unless atypical CNS features (encephalopathy, seizures) are present.
Echocardiography is not indicated in typical GBS; reserve for pre-existing cardiac disease or unexplained hemodynamic instability after autonomic causes are excluded.
Head CT contributes no diagnostic information in GBS; the disease is peripheral and CT does not visualise nerve roots reliably.
Functional / metabolic brain imaging adds no value in a peripheral demyelinating syndrome.
Cerebrovascular imaging is not indicated in a peripheral neuropathy without focal cerebral signs.
Brain MRI is reserved for atypical features (encephalopathy, CNS signs, transverse myelitis on differential). In classic GBS it does not aid diagnosis.

patient.chief_complaint: Seven-day rapidly progressive ascending paralysis and areflexia, preceded by diarrheal illness. SpO2 92% on room air — respiratory failure imminent.
patient.history_present_illness: Mr. A. is a 28-year-old restaurant worker presenting with rapidly progressive ascending weakness over 7 days. He had bloody diarrhea 3 weeks ago, lasting 5 days, consistent with Campylobacter (no stool culture obtained but presentation classic). Seven days ago, he noticed tingling in his feet. Weakness ascended rapidly — he could not walk 3 days ago, and now cannot move his legs at all. Bilateral facial drooping developed 2 days ago. He is now in respiratory distress with SpO2 92% on room air and FVC 41%. He is being brought emergently for ICU level care.
